# Using Leak Guard in Muse Code

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to Muse Code.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.agents/skills/leak-guard/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.agents/skills/leak-guard/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness muse --skill leak-guard
node packages/cli install --harness muse --skill leak-guard --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. Muse Code loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also name it in the request, for example: "Use the leak-guard skill to ...".

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.agents/skills/leak-guard` for a project install, or `~/.agents/skills/leak-guard` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Run `muse skills list` to see the skills Muse discovered.

## Notes

- Based on one community report: muse skills list scans ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills, and ~/.codex/skills.
- This skill drives packages/leakguard. Read scripts/leakguard.root for the absolute package path; if you copied the skill folder by hand without the install command, locate packages/leakguard in the gti-skills repository and use its bin/leakguard.mjs and bin/leakguard-hook.mjs paths.
- Unsupported: no documented pre-tool hook exists. This skill can only scan for earlier leaks here; do not attempt to install a guard into Muse.
- Documentation: [Muse Code](https://www.withone.ai/blog/muse-code-skills-not-mcp) (path source: community).
